title: Token Budgets: An Empirical Catalog of 63 LLM-Agent Budget-Overrun Incidents, with an Affine-Typed Rust Mitigation as a Case Study
authors: Sajjad Khan
problem: Prevent LLM-agent budget overruns and delegation double spend.
assumptions: Estimator upper bound holds; budget object remains inside one typed Rust process.
method: Affine Budget ownership with pre-flight spend reservation receipt and refund/reconciliation.
datasets: 63 incidents from 21 frameworks; live APIs across three providers; calibrated simulations.
baselines: Five runtime mitigations; locked Python counter; Agent Contracts; racy asyncio.
main_results: Reports zero cap violations in live tests; adaptive estimator reduces over-reservation relative to static.
limitations: No cross-process multi-tenant reservation; missing canceled-stream usage and hidden reasoning tokens remain open; no refinement proof.
gov_ar_difference: Closest liability work but lacks distributed tenant ledger joint routing and delayed settlement handling.
code_data: Artifact and Rust crate linked from arXiv.

title: ParetoBandit: Budget-Paced Adaptive Routing for Non-Stationary LLM Serving
authors: Annette Taberner-Miller
problem: Route online under dollar-rate targets and quality/price/model drift.
assumptions: Open-ended sequential stream; realized cost observed after inference; average cost constraint; deterministic model cost estimate at selection.
method: LinUCB with primal-dual budget pacer geometric forgetting and hot-swap registry.
datasets: 1,824 holdout prompts from nine public benchmarks; three-model portfolio.
baselines: Static/offline routers; bandit without closed-loop budget control; fixed-model policies.
main_results: Reports budget compliance within 0.4 percent and adaptation to price/quality shifts.
limitations: Empirical rather than hard-window guarantee; no concurrent outstanding liabilities or settlement ledger.
gov_ar_difference: GOV-AR targets per-tenant hard windows and unresolved stochastic cost rather than long-run average rate.

title: R2-Router: A New Paradigm for LLM Routing with Reasoning
authors: Jiaqi Xue; Qian Lou; Jiarong Xing; Heng Huang
problem: Jointly select an LLM and controllable response-length budget.
assumptions: Length-constrained instruction affects quality/cost predictably over benchmark operating points.
method: Reasoning router explores model and output-budget pairs; introduces R2-Bench.
datasets: R2-Bench: over 30,000 queries from six major benchmarks and multiple length budgets.
baselines: Prior reactive routers and fixed model-cost operating points.
main_results: Reports state-of-the-art routing at four-to-five-times lower cost in evaluated settings.
limitations: Controls requested output budget; does not reserve uncertain monetary liability or settle concurrency.
gov_ar_difference: Precludes any first joint model/output-budget claim; GOV-AR's distinction is stochastic reserve-settle.
code_data: Code and R2-Bench linked in paper.

title: Adaptive LLM Routing under Budget Constraints
authors: Pranoy Panda; Raghav Magazine; Chaitanya Devaguptapu; Sho Takemori; Vishal Sharma
problem: Adapt routing from partial feedback while respecting user budgets.
assumptions: Bandit feedback from selected model; multi-choice knapsack cost policy; learned shared query/model embedding.
method: PILOT extends LinUCB with offline preference prior and online refinement.
datasets: Public multi-LLM routing and preference datasets listed in paper.
baselines: Supervised routers; LinUCB variants; fixed and budget routing baselines.
main_results: Reports improved cost-aware routing from partial feedback.
limitations: Finite-horizon/knapsack abstraction does not model output-cost uncertainty or reserve-settle faults.
gov_ar_difference: Required published budget-router baseline; GOV-AR adds liability accounting and governance feasibility.

authors: Fangzhou Wu; Sandeep Silwal

datasets: Three benchmark datasets.
baselines: Eight routing baselines.
main_results: Reports average gains in performance cost efficiency and throughput and a 1-o(1) competitive ratio under assumptions.

gov_ar_difference: Strong online baseline but orthogonal to outstanding-cost safety.

authors: Iqtedar Uddin; Andre Bauer

baselines: Validation-tuned routing threshold and fixed routes.

datasets: Theoretical instances and simulations in supplement.
baselines: Prior adversarial and stochastic delayed-bandit algorithms.
main_results: Provides near-optimal guarantees in both regimes under stated delay knowledge.
limitations: Feedback delay affects learning but there is no unsettled financial resource.
gov_ar_difference: Foundation only; not a reserve-settle protocol.

title: Approximately Stationary Bandits with Knapsacks
authors: Giannis Fikioris; Eva Tardos
problem: Budgeted bandits between stochastic and adversarial extremes.
assumptions: Approximate stationarity parameters characterize deviation and budget size.
method: Algorithms whose competitive guarantee interpolates between regimes.
datasets: Theoretical problem families.
baselines: Stochastic BwK and adversarial BwK algorithms.
main_results: Derives approximately tight transition guarantees especially for small budgets.
limitations: No contexts in core result and no concurrent settlement.
gov_ar_difference: Supports drift-aware budget theory background but not LLM ledger novelty.

title: Bandits with Knapsacks and Predictions
authors: Davide Drago; Andrea Celli; Marek Elias
problem: Exploit predictions in BwK without losing worst-case robustness.
assumptions: Static prediction quality and Slater-style feasibility govern improved ratios.
method: Learning-augmented algorithms combining predictions with robust no-regret routines.
datasets: Theoretical and numerical settings in paper.
baselines: Primal-dual BwK algorithms without predictions.
main_results: Provides improved ratios/regret with accurate predictions and fallback guarantees with poor predictions.
limitations: Does not address stochastic unknown cost tails or transaction state.
gov_ar_difference: Supports conservative fallback concept as known learning-augmented machinery.
code_data: No code link stated on PMLR page.

title: Conformal Risk Control
authors: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos; Stephen Bates; Adam Fisch; Lihua Lei; Tal Schuster
problem: Control expected monotone loss with finite calibration data.
assumptions: Exchangeable calibration/test examples and monotone bounded loss; extensions require additional conditions.
method: Generalizes split conformal calibration to risk-controlling parameter selection.
datasets: Computer vision and NLP worked examples.
baselines: Split conformal and task-specific threshold tuning.
main_results: Shows expected-risk control tight up to an order 1/n factor under assumptions.
limitations: Exchangeability can fail under routing selection and drift; not an instantaneous concurrent union bound by itself.
gov_ar_difference: Risk control is known; GOV-AR must state conditional history/predictable allocation assumptions.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
authors: Isaac Gibbs; Emmanuel Candes
problem: Maintain long-run coverage frequency under unknown temporal distribution shift.
assumptions: Online sequential outcomes; coverage target updated through one-dimensional online learning.
method: Adaptive conformal alpha update wrapping arbitrary point/quantile predictor.
datasets: Stock volatility and COVID-style time-series examples described in paper.
baselines: Static conformal prediction and fixed intervals.
main_results: Proves long-run coverage-frequency control and reports robustness to visible shifts.
limitations: Long-run marginal frequency is not per-time conditional risk; rapid drift can cause transient failure.
gov_ar_difference: Supports adaptation background but cannot justify instantaneous liability guarantee.

title: Conformal Inference for Online Prediction with Arbitrary Distribution Shifts
authors: Isaac Gibbs; Emmanuel J. Candes
problem: Adapt conformal prediction to arbitrary and locally varying distribution shifts.
assumptions: Sequential prediction and a comparator path whose local variation determines regret.
method: Adaptive step-size procedure with local interval regret.
datasets: Stock-market volatility and COVID-19 case-count data.
baselines: Adaptive Conformal Inference and static conformal methods.
main_results: Provides local regret/coverage adaptation results and empirical robustness.
limitations: Still gives online aggregate behavior rather than guaranteed conditional coverage at every selected request.
gov_ar_difference: Supports visible drift/fallback requirement; does not solve settlement.
code_data: JMLR PDF and BibTeX; code status in paper.

title: Stochastic Model Predictive Control with Joint Chance Constraints
authors: Joel A. Paulson; Edward A. Buehler; Richard D. Braatz; Ali Mesbah
problem: Optimize control under joint probabilistic state constraints.
assumptions: Linear dynamics; arbitrary disturbances represented by mean/variance; Cantelli-Chebyshev surrogate.
method: Iterative convex programs jointly choose feedback gain and risk allocation.
datasets: Continuous acetone-butanol-ethanol fermentation case study.
baselines: Fixed/uniform risk allocation and deterministic/robust MPC alternatives.
main_results: Demonstrates tractable joint chance-control and optimized risk allocation in the case study.
limitations: Risk allocation is conservative and application assumptions differ from LLM tail calibration.
gov_ar_difference: Shows allocation of a global risk budget among concurrent constraints is known generally.
code_data: No code/data link stated on publisher page.

title: The Escrow Transactional Method
authors: Patrick E. O'Neil
problem: Permit long-lived concurrent updates while preserving numeric integrity constraints.
assumptions: Updates admit escrowable bounds and database recovery/commit mechanisms.
method: Reserve portions of a numeric resource before asynchronous commit or abort.
datasets: Database transaction examples including inventory/reservation.
baselines: Long locks; hotspot concurrency methods; conventional transactions.
main_results: Shows nonblocking long-lived resource reservation with recoverable intermediate guarantees.
limitations: Predates LLMs and probabilistic cost; no model routing or telemetry semantics.
gov_ar_difference: Reserve/release and invariant preservation are established database ideas not GOV-AR novelty.
code_data: No code; formal algorithm in article.

title: A Survey on Transactional Stream Processing
authors: Shuhao Zhang; Juan Soto; Volker Markl
problem: Taxonomize transaction and stream guarantees under concurrency failures and event delivery.
assumptions: System guarantees vary by transaction/event model; exactly-once commonly means consistent recovery rather than literal single delivery.
method: Survey taxonomy of transactional stream processing requirements and systems.
datasets: Six representative TSP systems and published use cases.
baselines: STREAM; FlowDB; TSPoon; Flink-related and other transactional stream systems.
main_results: Identifies design trade-offs for ACID state event ordering duplicates and recovery.
limitations: Survey rather than new mechanism; no LLM-specific budget semantics.
gov_ar_difference: Supports idempotent duplicate/out-of-order settlement design as known systems practice.
code_data: Open-access article; no single code artifact.

title: Dominant Resource Fairness: Fair Allocation of Multiple Resource Types
authors: Ali Ghodsi; Matei Zaharia; Benjamin Hindman; Andy Konwinski; Scott Shenker; Ion Stoica
problem: Fairly allocate heterogeneous resources among users with different demand vectors.
assumptions: Divisible resources and declared per-task demand vectors; cooperative scheduler.
method: Dominant Resource Fairness generalizes max-min fairness.
datasets: Mesos cluster experiments and synthetic demand mixes.
baselines: Slot fairness and alternative multi-resource allocations.
main_results: Proves sharing incentive strategy-proofness envy-freeness and Pareto efficiency; reports throughput/fairness benefits.
limitations: Resource allocation metric is not money-window liability and assumptions may not hold for priorities/governance.
gov_ar_difference: Fair allocation is established; GOV-AR must define financial isolation rather than claim generic fairness novelty.
code_data: Paper and slides publicly available through USENIX.

title: Learn then Test: Calibrating Predictive Algorithms to Achieve Risk Control
authors: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos; Stephen Bates; Emmanuel J. Candes; Michael I. Jordan; Lihua Lei
problem: Calibrate arbitrary predictive algorithms to finite-sample risk guarantees.
assumptions: Calibration and test data satisfy the testing assumptions for valid p-values; risk family and multiple-testing procedure are prespecified.
method: Reframes risk calibration as multiple hypothesis testing.
datasets: Computer-vision and tabular-medical worked examples.
baselines: Uncalibrated thresholds and standard calibration alternatives.
main_results: Provides finite-sample guarantees for several risks without retraining under assumptions.
limitations: Selection/adaptive routing can invalidate calibration if not represented; does not allocate concurrent financial risk.
gov_ar_difference: Further establishes risk calibration as known and motivates prespecified tests.
code_data: Supplement and code availability stated by authors.

title: Highly Available Transactions: Virtues and Limitations
authors: Peter Bailis; Aaron Davidson; Alan Fekete; Ali Ghodsi; Joseph M. Hellerstein; Ion Stoica
problem: Characterize transactional guarantees achievable with high availability during partitions.
assumptions: Asynchronous partition-prone replicated storage and a formal response-based availability definition.
method: Taxonomy impossibility results and proof-of-concept highly available transaction algorithms.
datasets: Wide-area prototype experiments and consistency models.
baselines: Serializable/snapshot isolation; master; two-phase locking; weak consistency.
main_results: Identifies which ACID/consistency properties are HAT-compliant and reports large WAN performance benefits with semantic compromises.
limitations: Global invariant enforcement and serializability require coordination/unavailability in relevant cases.
gov_ar_difference: Clarifies why GOV-AR should prefer a transactional primary ledger over claiming partition-available hard budget safety.
code_data: Extended version and prototype description available.

title: Acto: Automatic End-to-End Testing for Operation Correctness of Cloud System Management
authors: Jiawei Tyler Gu; Xudong Sun; Wentao Zhang; Yuxuan Jiang; Chen Wang; Mandana Vaziri; Owolabi Legunsen; Tianyin Xu
problem: Automatically test Kubernetes operators together with their managed systems.
assumptions: Declarative state-reconciliation interfaces expose state/actions and test oracles can be synthesized from operation semantics.
method: State-centric end-to-end test generation and execution.
datasets: Eleven Kubernetes operators and their managed systems.
baselines: Existing operator/unit/e2e testing practices.
main_results: Reports 56 serious new bugs with 42 confirmed and 30 fixed at publication.
limitations: Does not test application-specific financial invariants without supplied semantics.
gov_ar_difference: Establishes operator correctness testing as known; GOV-AR should use its fault/state lessons.
code_data: Acto artifact availability documented by authors.

title: Automatic Reliability Testing for Cluster Management Controllers
authors: Xudong Sun; Wenqing Luo; Jiawei Tyler Gu; Aishwarya Ganesan; Ramnatthan Alagappan; Michael Gasch; Lalith Suresh; Tianyin Xu
problem: Find safety and liveness bugs in reconciliation-based cluster controllers.
assumptions: Controllers should tolerate admissible perturbations of their observed cluster state; reference and perturbed runs are comparable.
method: Sieve systematically perturbs controller/API observations and compares state evolution.
datasets: Ten popular Kubernetes controllers.
baselines: Existing controller tests and manually injected faults.
main_results: Reports 46 serious bugs with 35 confirmed and 22 fixed and 3.5 percent false-positive rate.
limitations: Differential oracle can miss bugs common to both executions and needs representative workloads.
gov_ar_difference: Required controller reliability precedent; GOV-AR fault campaign must be invariant-specific and state-centric.
code_data: Public Sieve artifact linked by USENIX.
